Besides the app itself, a theme colours the code in Claude's replies, the diffs in Changes and in the conversation, and the terminal panel. Every [built-in theme](/themes/built-in/) brings its own code colours, and a [theme file](/themes/custom/) can set them too.

<Screenshot name="code-block" alt="A code block in Claude's reply with syntax colours: keywords, strings and comments each in their own colour on the code background" width={720} eager />

## Where to find it

- The colours follow the theme you pick in **Settings → Theme** (<Kbd shortcut="settings" />) or with *Theme: &lt;name&gt;* in the command palette.
- When you import a theme, the preview shows a code sample in its code colours (with the name of the syntax theme it uses) and its 16 terminal colours.
- **Settings → Diagnostics** shows a code block and some Markdown under **Rendering**, in the theme in use.

## Code colours

Code blocks always sit on the theme's `code-bg` colour, never on the background of the syntax theme. Light and dark mode each have their own code colours, and they switch with the app.

In a theme file, `syntax` in a mode sets them. It is one of:

- **The name of a syntax theme that comes with Seshboard**, such as `github-dark`, `dracula`, `nord`, `one-dark-pro`, `solarized-light` or `tokyo-night`. The full list is in [Code colours](https://github.com/estruyf/switchboard/blob/main/docs/themes.md#code-colours). A name that isn't on the list refuses the file, with a hint when it looks like a typo.
- **Your own colours**, such as the `tokenColors` of a VS Code theme. Only `name`, `type` and `tokenColors` are read, and of each rule only its `scope`, `foreground` colour and `fontStyle` (`italic`, `bold`, `underline`).

```json
"syntax": {
  "name": "Mine",
  "type": "dark",
  "tokenColors": [
    { "scope": ["comment"], "settings": { "foreground": "#7f8c98", "fontStyle": "italic" } },
    { "scope": ["keyword", "storage"], "settings": { "foreground": "#ff7ab2" } },
    { "scope": "string", "settings": { "foreground": "#a3e635" } }
  ]
}
```

Without `syntax`, code keeps Demo Time's colours.

## Diffs

Added and removed lines take their background from the `diff-added` and `diff-removed` tokens, and their marks from `ok` and `error`. Without them, a theme generates the backgrounds from `ok` and `error`.

## Terminal colours

<Screenshot name="terminal" alt="A session with the terminal panel open below the conversation, dark, with coloured shell output" />

The terminal panel is always dark, in light mode too, so a theme sets its colours once, in `dark.terminal`:

| Key | What it sets |
|---|---|
| `background` | the terminal's background (and the panel around it, unless `colors.terminal-bg` says otherwise) |
| `foreground` | its text |
| `cursor` | the cursor |
| `selection` | selected text |
| `ansi` | exactly 16 colours: black, red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan, white, then the bright versions in the same order |

```json
"terminal": {
  "background": "#001e26",
  "foreground": "#93a1a1",
  "cursor": "#b58900",
  "ansi": ["#073642", "#dc322f", "#859900", "#b58900", "#268bd2", "#d33682", "#2aa198", "#eee8d5",
           "#002b36", "#cb4b16", "#586e75", "#657b83", "#839496", "#6c71c4", "#93a1a1", "#fdf6e3"]
}
```

Each key is optional. Without it, the terminal uses the dark mode's `terminal-bg`, `text` and `accent-ink`, the accent at 25% for the selection, and Demo Time's 16 colours.

<Aside>
Terminal and code colours go through the same check as the rest of a theme: colour values only.
</Aside>

## Settings

Code and terminal colours come with the theme you choose in [Settings → Theme](/settings/#theme). There is no separate setting for them.
